solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Girl invited outside welcomes hour recalling 9

indicators.note: recalling means calling back, so the assembled letters are read backwards
the girl's name takes the hour abbreviation in, as a host welcomes a guest

parts.note: Maud is the girl summoned out into the garden in Tennyson's famous poem and song

explanation.surface: A girl asked out into the garden lets in an hour of memories of a city she knows.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' is a cross-reference to 9 down, the puzzle's theme: each themed answer is an example of it. 'recalling' turns MAHRUD round.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is the cross-referenced 9 down; this northern English city has a famous Norman cathedral.

clue.text: 1 down's tricky? Deny responsibility!

indicators.note: tricky signals the letters are juggled into a new order

parts.note: the figure 1 is read as the letter I, giving I, DOWN and S

explanation.surface: A setter complains that 1 down is tricky and refuses any blame.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 down' looks like a self-reference to the clue's own number; read as I DOWN S, it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse to acknowledge anything as yours is to reject accountability, a close synonym.

clue.text: Pound, depleted, went off course

parts.note: to ram is to pound or strike hard
bled means drained or depleted, as resources bled dry

explanation.surface: A currency, weakened, drifted from its path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' tempts as sterling but is the verb, to batter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ramble is to wander aimlessly or stray from the subject, so it means deviated.

clue.text: DIY no use during disarray when erecting screen

indicators.note: erecting means setting upright, so in a down entry the letters are read upwards
the letters of DIY are of no use, so they are struck out of the longer word

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: Home improvement proves useless amid chaos while putting up a partition.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing D, I and Y from DISARRAY leaves SARRA; 'when erecting' turns it upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall tapestry, named after a French town, often hung as a curtain or divider, so it is a screen.

clue.text: Recklessly pursued, run away exhausted

indicators.note: done recklessly, the letters of the word pursued are thrown into a new order, with the run letter going away from them

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone chased hard by a pursuer flees and ends up worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: 'Recklessly' rearranges PURSUED, and 'run away' says R (cricket's run) is the letter left over, leaving six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean completely spent or drained of energy or supply; an adjectival phrase synonym.

clue.text: 9 perhaps absorbing Irish city of no note

indicators.note: the word for perhaps takes the trimmed city into its middle

parts.note: say, as in for example, means perhaps

indicators.note: of no note means the note letter is removed

parts.note: Lisburn is a city in Northern Ireland, near Belfast

explanation.surface: A cathedral town perhaps taking in an obscure Irish city.
explanation.walkthrough: '9 perhaps' hints at the definition, but 'perhaps' is SAY; 9 alone defines. 'of no note' looks like 'obscure' but drops the N from LISBURN.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme entry: the Wiltshire city whose cathedral has England's tallest spire.

clue.text: Originates campaigns about Ecstasy

indicators.note: the campaigns go about, around, the drug letter

parts.note: drives are organised campaigns, as in a recruitment drive
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug campaign has its roots in efforts concerning ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that derives from a source comes from it, so derive means stem or arise.

clue.text: Scourge — somewhat like paronomasia?

parts.note: paronomasia is the formal term for wordplay on similar-sounding words
the suffix -ish means somewhat like, as in reddish

explanation.surface: A scourge that is a bit like a play on words.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a whip, and to scourge is to inflict harsh correction, as a penalty.

clue.text: Wine sends compiler off to see quack

indicators.note: the compiler is sent off, so those letters are removed from the wine

parts.note: Medoc is a red Bordeaux wine
the compiler, the crossword setter, refers to himself as ME

explanation.surface: A setter's bottle of wine sends him to a dubious doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sends ... off' takes ME out of MEDOC.
explanation.definitionFit: Quack is informal slang for any doctor, not only a charlatan, and the short form is a casual name for a physician.

clue.text: Uncouple damaged air ducts and isolate, so not functional

indicators.note: damaged signals the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as part of the fodder

indicators.note: the word so is not working here, so it is taken out of isolate

parts.note: taken as written, the two letters to drop

explanation.surface: Disconnect broken air ducts and isolate them so they stop working.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing S and O from ISOLATE leaves ILATE; 'damaged' shuffles AIR DUCTS with ILATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate at a joint, a surgical or anatomical term, so it means detach or disconnect.

clue.text: Herding 101 hardy cattle — Hereford, maybe?

indicators.note: herding rounds the letters up and drives them into a new arrangement

parts.note: 101 in Roman numerals is CI
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rounding up 101 tough cows: are they Herefords?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hereford' looks like the cattle breed; it is the English city with a cathedral. 'Herding' shuffles CI, HARDY and CATTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereford, on the River Wye, is an English city whose cathedral houses the Mappa Mundi, an example of the type.

clue.text: Acting with spirit, amateur is about to give back retainer

indicators.note: about signals turning round, here the short word for acting

parts.note: acting as someone is standing in for them, so acting gives AS

indicators.note: giving back means returning, so the spirit is read backwards

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane
I is the first letter standing in for is

explanation.surface: An amateur actor, fortified by drink, is about to return a fee paid in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: AS and RUM are each read backwards (SA, MUR); the blogger called the wordplay clumsy. 'Retainer' is a sense of the noun, a sworn follower, not the fee the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A samurai was a Japanese warrior retained in the service of a feudal lord, a retainer in the old sense of household follower.

clue.text: Flap on air led shortly to sack

indicators.note: to sack is to plunder and wreck, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: shortly means the word is clipped, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before being cut short

explanation.surface: An on-air broadcast flap quickly leads to someone being fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts LED to LE; 'to sack' then shuffles ON, AIR and LE together.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is a hinged flap on an aircraft wing that controls roll.

clue.text: Issues for 9

definitions.meaning: comes up or flows out, as water rising from a spring
the cross-referenced theme entry: a Somerset city with a cathedral, England's smallest city

explanation.surface: Problems arising over a city.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to issue is to flow out, and liquid that rises up does this; the Somerset city is also named for its springs.

clue.text: Tacky items she performs In adult nightclubs

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed in the seedy clubs

parts.note: dives are seedy nightclubs or bars

indicators.note: the woman performs, acting the word she out into a new order

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: A tawdry list of things a woman does on stage in adult nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performs' rearranges the letters of 'she'. 'Tacky' looks like an insult but means sticky.
explanation.definitionFit: Glues and pastes are sticky substances, and tacky means sticky, so tacky items is a playful description.

clue.text: Letter about old coin, having uranium in rim, offers informed speculation

indicators.note: the letter's name goes around the coin and rim pieces

parts.note: ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S
the ducat was a gold or silver coin used across Europe

indicators.note: the uranium symbol goes inside the word for rim

parts.note: an edge is a rim or border
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A letter discusses an antique coin with uranium in its rim, offering a learned guess about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' is the spelt-out name of S, which splits E...SS around the coin and the enlarged rim.
explanation.definitionFit: A guess based on knowledge and reasoning is speculation backed by information, so the phrase is a close synonym.

clue.text: Brownie's 4 in bafflement

indicators.note: 4 across reads used up, so in this down entry the letters are read upwards
the letters sit in the middle of the longer word

explanation.surface: A young Brownie's bafflement.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 4 across (USED UP) is the reversal: FLE, inside 'bafflement', is read upwards. The blogger found this a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A brownie is a small helpful household goblin of folklore, a kind of sprite; Brownie packs also have groups called Elves.

clue.text: Record setter's impulsive in making quick descent

indicators.note: the impulsive word goes in the record

parts.note: CD, compact disc, is a record
rash means impulsive or hasty
setter's stands for setter has, I have, contracted to I've

explanation.surface: The compiler is reckless in setting a record for a fast drop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter's' means 'the setter has', I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine's emergency plunge below the surface is a rapid dive, a fast descent.

clue.text: 'Ecclesiastical' gentleman?

definitions.meaning: the courtesy title once given to priests
the respectful form of address for a man, or a knight's title

explanation.definitionFit: The title was formerly used for clergy and is still the polite address to any man or a knight's honorific.

clue.text: 'Cranefly', in a first-class condition, goes from 6/4 to 5/4

indicators.note: condition here is the verb, to treat or shape, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, the insect name used as letters
taken as written
A1, written AI, means first-class

explanation.surface: A daddy-long-legs in top condition whose odds drift from 6/4 to 5/4.
explanation.walkthrough: The dates look like betting odds; they are 6 April to 5 April, the span of the UK tax and accounting period. 'condition' shuffles CRANEFLY, IN A and AI.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the tax period runs from 6 April to 5 April, so it is defined by its start and end dates.

clue.text: Incorporate here a bit of deception?

definitions.text: Incorporate here a bit of deception?

indicators.note: incorporate means take inside, so one letter is put into the phrase

parts.note: here, the place you are reading, is in clue

indicators.note: a bit of means just the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A setter mischievously suggests slipping a little trickery into this clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' is read as IN CLUE, and 'Incorporate' puts D, the first letter of 'deception', inside it before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: To incorporate is to take something in as part of a whole, the exact sense of add or embrace.

clue.text: Snake having rest on road surface

parts.note: the asp is a venomous snake, Cleopatra's
a halt is a rest or stop

explanation.surface: A snake basking on the tarmac.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmac-like bitumen mix is the black material laid to pave roads.

clue.text: Much name-dropping by green ex-VP?

indicators.note: the name drops a letter from one place to another, so a single letter shifts position

parts.note: Al Gore, US vice-president under Clinton, is known for environmental campaigning

explanation.surface: Lots of name-dropping by an environmentalist former vice-president.
explanation.walkthrough: The blogger was baffled too: 'name-dropping' seems to mean the name AL GORE is dropped into a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed after a noun, it means in abundance or plenty, so it equals much or many.

clue.text: Learnt to play the horn

indicators.note: to play with letters is to toss them about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone learned how to play the French horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horn' looks like a musical instrument but is a deer's branched growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag's branched bony outgrowth is loosely called a horn.

clue.text: Rector leaves local choir drunk in boozer!

the rector leaves, so his letter is taken out of the phrase

explanation.surface: The rector walks out after the parish singers get drunk in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozer' tempts as the British word for a pub (the surface's 'in boozer') but is the definition, a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A boozer is someone who drinks heavily, a person addicted to drink.

clue.text: 9 with death wish and no comeback?

explanation.definitionFit: The theme entry: a North Yorkshire city with a cathedral, among the smallest cities in England.

clue.text: Bailiff to attach rope to the 'Sandpiper'

definitions.meaning: a medieval steward or local magistrate who managed an estate
a sailing term: to pass a line through a ring or block and fasten it
the female of the ruff, a wading bird of the sandpiper family

clue.text: He gets a sight 28

clue.text: Mycelia neotoxin returns, its focus on the foot

explanation.definitionFit: Toenails grow on the toes, a feature found on the foot; the blogger thought the definition loose.

clue.text: Recovering gambler?

one who bets or wagers money
